title: Book One · Chapter 15: A Small Promise
story:
On Monday, Ronan and Leo take the kite picture to school.

Their real kite stays on the board at home. It isn't ready for the class display. Ronan thinks they can finish it soon. It has a tail now. Kites need tails. He feels sure the tail will help.

Mei looks at their drawing.

"I like that blue," she says.

"There are three blues," Ronan tells her.

"Then I like three blues."

A boy called Jun comes over. He is from the row by the door. His shirt pocket has a little hole. He puts one finger through it while he looks at the drawing.

"Can you make one for me?"

Leo opens his mouth, but Ronan speaks first.

"Yes."

"When?"

"Before class day."

Leo looks at him. Ronan keeps looking at Jun.

Jun has a coin in his other hand. "My mum said I could use this for something small."

Ronan feels the coin touch his palm. It is warm. He thinks of the tea box at home.

Miss Wu sees the three boys around the desk.

"What are we doing here?"

Jun tells her. Ronan closes his hand and opens it again.

Miss Wu sits beside them. "No buying or taking money in class. Did both your parents agree to this?"

Jun shakes his head. Ronan says nothing.

"Then the coin goes home with Jun today."

Ronan gives it back. Jun looks disappointed, but he puts it in the pocket without the hole.

After school, Miss Wu speaks to Mum at the gate. "The display is free," she says. The parents can talk about a kite at home. They must agree before money changes hands. This is not part of the class day. "You can all come and look for free."

On the way home, Mum asks Ronan, "Can your kite fly yet?"

"Nearly."

"What does nearly mean?"

"It has a tail now."

"Did you try to fly it with the tail?"

"Not yet."

Mum stops at the fruit shop to choose two soft pears. Ronan stands beside her. He said yes to Jun at once. But the kite needs a lot of work. He looks at his fingers. There is still dry paste on one.

That evening, Jun and his mother come to the green gate. Jun's mother has heard about the kite. She asks to see it.

Ronan brings it out carefully.

"It's your first one?" she asks.

"Yes."

Jun still wants one. The two mothers make a plan. Jun gives one small coin for paper and paste. Mum will keep it separate. Ronan may fail to make the kite. Then Mum will give the coin back. Ronan will not earn money from it. The money is not for school.

"Are you sure?" Mum asks Ronan.

He looks at Jun's happy face.

"Yes. By class day."

Mum writes their plan on a piece of paper. She puts the coin in a small folded packet, away from Ronan's own three coins.

They leave the house. Leo and his father are waiting outside. Leo came to ask about trying the tail.

"You said yes," he tells Ronan quietly.

"I can make another."

"This kite is not finished yet."

Ronan lifts the tail. All three blues hang down. He wants Jun to fly a kite beside theirs. He counts the new pieces of paper for Jun's kite. He does not count the work hours yet.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：agree＝同意；packet＝小纸包；nearly＝差不多；coin＝硬币。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 答应给谁做风筝？
2. 一枚硬币为什么不能直接留在课桌里？
